method: Same AI, separate source-first pass after freezing. Re-extracted the dated UvA curriculum table and track and year-progression material. Confirmed independent thesis research and its separate skills course, the open semester and the specialist valuation and reserving progression. Started from the current workbook descriptions, topics and course dependencies to re-evaluate the UCR probability, regression, financial and risk contributions before comparing the frozen record.
findings: The official curriculum for 2026–2027 and dated catalogue identify one 180 EC full-time degree with substantively identical English and Dutch tracks, so no language variant is selected for the generic target. Both first and second years comprise ten 6 EC courses. The third year has a 30 EC choice space followed by five 6 EC components. An internship is combined with electives. The thesis comprises distinct research and skills components worth 6 EC each.

The normal sequence completes 60 EC in year 1, exceeding the current 48 EC binding-study-advice threshold. Calculus, linear algebra, probability, economics and programming support advanced mathematics, econometrics, machine learning and life insurance in year 2. Risk Theory and the research seminar precede the year-3 specialisation. The normal plan completes 150 EC before the final semester, when insurance accounting, stochastic life models, finance and the two thesis components occur. The preceding 2025–2026 regulations corroborate the 120 EC threshold for both separately coded thesis components and the internship-plus-electives arrangement. The 2026–2027 study page governs current structure; the earlier OER is used only as historical corroboration, not to assert a current threshold.

The principal overlap is the combination of quantitative uncertainty and financial applications. UCR covers distributions, inference and simulation, Bayesian and Markov decision models, regression, numerical methods, predictive validation, asset pricing, interest-rate exposure, bank capital and liquidity. These are substantive tools and applications for studying risk. Public Economics treats social insurance as policy, not actuarial valuation. Database Management Systems provides a supported description-only contribution in SQL, relational modelling and data preparation, rather than alignment to introductory actuarial science. Description-only Advanced Calculus, Behavioral Economics and Econometrics contribute multivariable analysis, actual decision behaviour and applied regression, respectively. Behavioral Economics moves to the final autumn. Computational & Numerical Methods and Optimization Methods in AI replace two broader business selections and add convergence, approximation and constrained optimisation. Early programming and linear algebra support later work. No workbook sequence teaches insurance pricing and reserving, life contingencies and pension liabilities. A second data-centred schedule with algorithms, deep learning and reinforcement learning would duplicate the useful methods while losing financial applications, and a policy-focused programme would lose quantitative risk. Neither offers a second substantiated response to the exact target. All positive pairings were tested against the external course descriptions or explicit programme subjects; general databases are no longer paired to the actuarial introduction.
